description: b9d's getBlock truncation handling: the fix that keeps one cut-mid-stream response out of tens of thousands from killing a multi-day stage. Guards that a decode failure is RETRIED (not fatal on first), that the failure is INSPECTED and labelled truncated-vs-malformed rather than reported as a plain transport failure, and -- the reviewer's declared concern -- that the last attempt RAISES with that detail and never falls through to a half-parsed result.

mutants.name: a decode failure is fatal on the first attempt again
mutants.note: Never retries the decode, so the truncated-then-whole body raises on attempt 1 instead of recovering; test_a_truncated_getblock_body_is_retried_then_returns_the_whole_response fails.

mutants.name: the last attempt is swallowed into a half-parsed result
mutants.note: The reviewer's declared mutant: on exhaustion it returns the truncated body with an empty result instead of raising -- worse than the fatal it replaced. test_the_last_attempt_raises_it_is_never_swallowed_into_a_partial_result fails because nothing is raised.

mutants.name: the truncated/malformed inspection is dropped
mutants.old: kind = "truncated transfer" if short_of_declared or failed_at_end else "malformed body"
mutants.note: Every undecodable body is called a truncation, so a genuinely malformed body from a broken provider is mislabelled; test_a_malformed_full_body_is_labelled_malformed_not_truncated fails.

expected_survivors_note: None. Each mutant breaks one of the three properties the fix exists for -- retry, honest labelling, and raise-not-swallow -- and each is killed by a RpcRetryTests case that drives rpc_request with an in-memory opener and no external artifact.
pytest_args_reason: The sweep scopes to RpcRetryTests, which exercises the transport retry loop with in-memory openers and needs no external artifact. The rest of the file is left in place; narrowing here is about which guards the score covers -- the truncation-retry path -- not about hiding a class that would fail. Every declared mutant lives in that path and is killed by those tests, so nothing killable only outside RpcRetryTests is claimed.
